push.title: D 2-2 vs itwasnt6million | You: 7.3 (7th worst match performance)
push.body:
Your 7th worst match performance, PhogsToffees: a 7.3. A dip, not a slide.

THE GOOD
+ 1 key pass. You found gaps I didn't know were there, and I was looking.
+ That link with BellyTb1 was smoother than a Cadillac on new pavement.
+ Top-rated Grizzly in the match. That's a habit, and habits win leagues.
+ Missed tackles 0, down from your usual 2. That doesn't happen by accident.
+ Team-high 2 shots. Nobody hands out trophies for that, so here's my handshake.

THE BAD
- 1 of 2 shots on target. A little secret: Tight angle? Cut it back to a teammate. A better shot beats a first shot. Patience, partner.
- 68% passing (19 of 28, down from your usual 79%). Think about this: Through balls only when the runner is already moving and on the last defender's shoulder. Next match, nail it.
- Tackles attempted 0, down from your usual 3. That's the part of the tape we'll rewind.
- 0.6 below your typical game. That's an outlier, not an identity.
- Key passes 1, from 4 in your previous match. It's a small thing until it's the whole thing.

Fundamentals drill: Hit the target first, beat the keeper second. A shot on target can still be saved into a rebound.

PhogsToffees, something I want you to sleep on: A coach's whistle is just a fancy way of saying 'I care.'

Keep the faith, partner. - Coach Lasso

push.title: D 2-2 vs itwasnt6million | You: 7.2 (5th worst match performance)
push.body:
Your 5th worst match performance, BellyTb1. A 7.2. Tomorrow's a better story.

THE GOOD
+ A goal against itwasnt6million, your 3rd straight match scoring. You found the corner like it owed you rent.
+ Fewest misplaced passes on the team (4). Proof you've got another gear.
+ 2-2 with itwasnt6million. Not bad, not great, very fixable.

THE BAD
- Only 15 passes (down from your usual 18). Pro tip: Check away, then check back. A two-yard feint buys you the space to receive. That's how good becomes great.
- Only 1 tackle attempted. Training homework: When the ball is lost, the nearest player presses and everyone else closes the passing lanes. Mind over matter.
- 7.2 goes down as your 5th worst match performance. Tomorrow writes a better line.
- You and tuxedo_slide both got caught on on-ball involvement. Fix it together: make triangles, 1-2 touch.
- Key passes: 0. Decent, but top-quarter midfielders get to 2+. That's the next rung.

Back-garden drill: Play with your head up between touches. You can't find a pass you never looked for.

Before you go, BellyTb1: Believe in yourself the way your dog believes in you.

The comeback starts now. - Coach Lasso

push.title: D 2-2 vs itwasnt6million | You: 6.8 (3rd worst match performance)
push.body:
tuxedo_slide, a 6.8, your 3rd worst match performance. Shake it off like a wet dog.

THE GOOD
+ 7 tackles attempted (up from your usual 2). You pressed like the ball owed you money.
+ A goal against itwasnt6million, your 3rd straight match scoring. Every team needs someone who smells goals. You've got the nose.
+ Level at 2-2 with itwasnt6million. Stalemates teach patience.

THE BAD
- Missed tackles 6, up from your usual 1. We can fix that.
- Rating came in 0.7 below what your on-ball stats earned. Easy win: Hold the line with your partner and step up together. Don't let a dropping striker drag you out.
- Team project for you and BellyTb1: on-ball involvement. The plan: make triangles, 1-2 touch.
- Key passes 0, down from your usual 1. Here's how: Switch play when they shift across. Quickest way to find space is usually on the far side.
- Shots 1, down from your usual 3. Here's the deal: When you've got a clear look inside the box, pull the trigger. Hesitation lets defenders recover.

THE UGLY
! Pass accuracy 54% (6 of 11). That's the stuff that keeps me up at night, and I sleep like a baby. Let's sharpen this: Pass to the far foot of a teammate who's facing play; it lets them take it forward in one touch.

Tonight's homework: Count your touches. Two-touch is a habit that keeps your head up and the ball moving.

Listen here, tuxedo_slide: Fall seven times, stand up eight, then ask for the ball.

Brick by brick. - Coach Lasso
